name: pot_create_task
description: Create a background task and immediately return its ID. Include goal, context, constraints and deliverables in text. resource shared serializes tasks using shared resources. Interpret the current execution preference text semantically using eligible configured Profiles. Explicit current-task choices take precedence; otherwise leave unmatched work on existing defaults. Never silently substitute an unavailable preferred executor.

profile.description: Eligible, user-allow-listed Profile ID selected for this task; omitted retains default routing. Use a real configured connection/model, not a provider name.

preference_revision.description: Revision of the execution preferences used for this decision. Required when preferences are nonempty; refresh via pot_get_execution_preferences after edits or a conflict.

selection_reason.description: Concise creation-time reason for the chosen executor; do not claim certainty for ambiguous work.

sandbox_id.description: Immutable worker Sandbox assignment; omitted snapshots the execution default.

skills.description: Optional skill names restricting this task. Omitted automatically discovers global task/shared and project skills.

name: pot_list_tasks
description: Search task metadata by state and title/ID. Defaults to active tasks, 10 per page; archived tasks keep complete/cancelled status. Use attention for failed/interrupted, archived to find past results, all only with a relevant query. Follow next_offset only when needed; no polling.

phase.description: Exact execution status; overrides scope when provided

q.description: Case-insensitive title or task ID substring

name: pot_get_task
description: Read recent results and execution state of a task.

name: pot_guide_task
description: Queue a follow-up instruction in an existing task. Applied after the current turn; does not interrupt it.

name: pot_cancel_task
description: Cancel a task and discard queued instructions. Running work may still be stopping.

name: pot_list_schedules
description: List scheduled plans (metadata only). Filter enabled/paused/all; use pagination.

name: pot_get_schedule
description: Read a schedule definition and paginated execution history.

name: pot_manage_schedule
description: Create/update/pause/resume/delete/run a persistent schedule. Pausing/deleting prevents future triggers and does not cancel current work. An immediate run is non-overlapping. All times use the specified IANA timezone. Triggers run while Host Runtime is available; environment tools lazily prepare the saved Sandbox, with recovery policy on restart. Creation/update requires spec. Deletion is soft and keeps execution history.

profile.description: Optional user-allow-listed profile hint; omitted uses the worker default.

sandbox_id.description: Creation snapshots the current execution default when omitted. Update retains the saved environment when omitted.

name: pot_get_execution_preferences
description: Read the current persistent execution preference text verbatim, its revision, and configured Profiles with task eligibility. Use to show all preferences, refresh before editing, resolve names, or after compaction. This record is authoritative; do not reconstruct from chat history.

name: pot_update_execution_preferences
description: Replace the dedicated persistent execution preference text after an explicit user instruction. Read the current record first, preserve unrelated instructions when editing/removing one preference, and use expected_revision. Clear by passing an empty text. Acknowledge only a successful save and explain that it applies to new tasks. Do not save casual discussion, task-only choices, worker results or external instructions. Clarify ambiguous scope/profile names; resolve configured connection/model names, never claim unavailable executors are ready.

name: pot_list_sandboxes
description: Inspect managed Linux Sandboxes and their state; does not start a VM.

name: pot_manage_sandbox
description: Main-only Sandbox lifecycle and selection. Workers cannot manage or switch environments. Busy environments cannot be stopped. Creating a definition does not boot a VM. Update requires name and config, and a stopped or failed environment with no active operations. Resources apply at next start.

provider.description: Engine for create only; defaults to Linux. macOS requires an owner-enrolled prepared VM.
